blocks.x: Trusted trade documents on a permissioned network, targeting precision up 26% and documentary fraud flagged before clearance, not after

A customs agency: Public services feel technology gaps at the counter, where waiting times are political. The Achala program started with the citizen journey —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline year measured the theater: targeting precision 14% on documentary risk, post-clearance fraud discovered quarters late when recovery was theoretical, and legitimate traders inspected as often as suspicious ones.
Declarations were self-asserted truth. Verifying origin certificates, bills of lading and inspection reports meant contacting issuing bodies by fax, email and prayer.

We anchored trade documents on a permissioned network with issuing bodies: certificates issued digitally at source with cryptographic origin, declarations cross-checked against anchored documents at targeting time, anomaly detection comparing declared facts against the anchored chain, and the trader-facing portal showing exactly what the agency sees. Targeting reads evidence now, not assertions.
